extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and host organisations applying to Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) under Horizon Europe
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting proposals to the MSCA calls under Horizon Europe (Doctoral Networks, Postdoctoral Fellowships, Staff Exchanges, COFUND, MSCA and Citizens, Choose Europe for Science, MSCA4Ukraine). Covers procedural requirements, scheme‑specific documents, evaluator matching, and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a profile on the Funding & tenders portal
rubrics_metrics.description: To apply, you must create a profile on the Funding & tenders portal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Then select the call for proposals you wish to apply for and use the proposal online form to submit your proposal before the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the proposal online form and submit before the deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Select the call and use the proposal online form on the portal to submit your proposal before the deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access the proposal online form (click 'Start submission' / 'Start submission' section / 'Start submission' link as indicated per call). Ensure submission is completed by the call deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check MSCA Work Programme and Guide for Applicants for scheme details
rubrics_metrics.description: For detailed information about each MSCA scheme, including eligibility conditions and implementation modalities, consult the corresponding sections in the MSCA Work Programme and the Guide for Applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different MSCA calls may have specific eligibility criteria regarding participation of organisations and countries. The legal text of the call takes precedence over summary pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the proposal template and instructions on how to fill it in
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the official proposal template and the instructions provided to complete your application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Template parts (e.g., Part B, Annex detailed budget table) and scheme-specific templates are referenced per call; follow them exactly to meet formatting/content expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select specific keywords in the proposal to aid evaluator matching
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to help the REA select appropriate expert evaluators, applicants will be asked to select specific keywords in the proposal template.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose keywords that reflect the proposal's expertise areas. For Staff Exchanges, these keywords should also be considered for proposals including interdisciplinary secondments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult MSCA-specific evaluation forms used by expert evaluators
rubrics_metrics.description: MSCA specific evaluation forms used by the expert evaluators are available and should be consulted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarity with the evaluation forms helps applicants understand the assessment dimensions experts will use (award criteria are defined in the Work Programme).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use scheme-specific guidance and preparatory materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the scheme-specific resources listed (e.g., Guide for Applicants, '6 steps to prepare your application', info session recordings, FAQs, informative flyers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resources are provided per scheme: Doctoral Networks, Postdoctoral Fellowships, Staff Exchanges, COFUND, MSCA and Citizens, Choose Europe for Science, MSCA4Ukraine. These include proposal templates, instructions, and common mistakes checklists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to scheme-specific eligibility metrics (example: Postdoctoral Fellowships 8‑year rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some schemes have specific eligibility calculations/metrics — e.g., Postdoctoral Fellowships include guidelines on the calculation of 8-years research experience and provide a self-assessment tool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the official guidelines and self-assessment tools to verify eligibility (especially for rules that depend on career stage/experience).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid known common mistakes (scheme-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consult resources such as 'Common mistakes in MSCA-PF proposal submission' to avoid typical errors that may harm your application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These documents identify anti-patterns and frequent submission pitfalls; follow them when preparing and checking your proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attend National Contact Point events and information days
rubrics_metrics.description: MSCA National Contact Points organise Information Days and events presenting the calls and helping applicants prepare successful proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact your national NCP for MSCA-related events and tailored help. Scheme-specific info days (e.g., Doctoral Networks Information Day) and recordings are available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult additional documents on the call page
rubrics_metrics.description: Any additional useful documents for a specific call can be found on that call's page on the Funding & tenders portal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Call pages aggregate annexes, templates, guides, and other supporting material — always check the call page for the authoritative package.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposals are evaluated by at least three independent external expert evaluators
rubrics_metrics.description: After the deadline, the REA organises an evaluation process: MSCA proposals are evaluated by at least 3 independent external expert evaluators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experts evaluate each proposal against the award criteria defined in the Work Programme. Being aware of these criteria and the evaluation forms is important for aligning your proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation timelines: evaluation lasts up to 5 months
rubrics_metrics.description: The evaluation phase lasts up to 5 months from the call deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for this timeframe when communicating with project partners and planning project start dates; applicants will be informed of results after evaluation completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant agreement preparation and signature timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: If successful, the REA launches grant agreement preparation with the successful applicants; generally the parties sign the grant agreement within 3 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult MSCA specific grant agreements under Horizon Europe reference documents to prepare for contractual obligations and implementation modalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use CORDIS and previously funded projects for inspiration
rubrics_metrics.description: You can find inspiration from previously funded projects in the CORDIS database.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review descriptions of funded projects to understand successful approaches, expected impacts, and implementation models, but rely on official call documents for requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal precedence and disclaimer
rubrics_metrics.description: The content of the informational page is for information purposes only; the relevant legal instruments and the text of the call shall take precedence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The European Commission and REA do not accept responsibility for any use made of the information on the page; always verify requirements against the official call text and legal documents.
